name: Mind, brain and society
dimension: the unit the claim is about

objects.label: Mental processes
objects.text: MS.O.A1 Mental processes

objects.label: Sensation and perception
objects.text: MS.O.A1.1 Sensation and perception. A stimulus is transduced; a percept is constructed. Named objects:

objects.label: Weber's law
objects.text: MS.O.A1.1.1 Weber's law: over a mid-range of intensities, the just-noticeable difference ΔI is a roughly constant fraction k of the base intensity I (Gescheider 1997).

objects.label: Fechner's law
objects.text: MS.O.A1.1.2 Fechner's law: if Weber's law holds and each JND is a unit step, sensation grows with the logarithm of intensity.

objects.label: Stevens's power law
objects.text: MS.O.A1.1.3 Stevens's power law: for direct magnitude estimation over a stated range, perceived magnitude is a power function of intensity.

objects.label: Signal detection theory
objects.text: MS.O.A1.1.4 Signal detection theory: under equal-variance Gaussian noise and signal distributions, d′ measures sensitivity and c (or β) measures criterion. A classical threshold confounds the two (Green and Swets 1966).

objects.label: Attention and consciousness
objects.text: MS.O.A1.2 Attention and consciousness. Selection has a cost; reportable experience has measurable conditions.

objects.label: Selective attention
objects.text: MS.O.A1.2.1 Selective attention and capacity limits; inattentional blindness.

objects.label: Consciousness as reportable experience
objects.text: MS.O.A1.2.2 Consciousness as reportable experience, studied with no-report controls. The hard problem is PL.O.A2; MS uses it and does not claim to solve it.

objects.label: Hypnosis and altered states
objects.text: MS.O.A1.2.3 Hypnosis and altered states, as changes in attention and report (APA Div. 30 home).

objects.label: Learning and memory
objects.text: MS.O.A1.3 Learning and memory.

objects.label: Classical conditioning; Rescorla–Wagner
objects.text: MS.O.A1.3.1 Classical conditioning: a cue comes to predict an outcome. Rescorla–Wagner model: on each trial, ΔV = αβ(λ − ΣV), where α and β are cue and outcome salience rates in (0,1], λ is the outcome's maximum, and ΣV sums all cues present.

objects.label: Operant conditioning
objects.text: MS.O.A1.3.2 Operant conditioning and schedules of reinforcement.

objects.label: Memory systems
objects.text: MS.O.A1.3.3 Memory systems: declarative (episodic, semantic) and nondeclarative (procedural, priming, classical conditioning, nonassociative) (Squire 2004).

objects.label: Working-memory capacity
objects.text: MS.O.A1.3.4 Working-memory capacity: about 3–5 chunks when rehearsal and chunking are blocked (Cowan 2001). The 7±2 figure is a heuristic (register).

objects.label: Forgetting
objects.text: MS.O.A1.3.5 Forgetting. Cue-dependent retrieval failure (Tulving 1974) is one answer. Interference, decay and failed consolidation are rivals (CONTESTED; Wixted 2004).

objects.label: Emotion and motivation
objects.text: MS.O.A1.4 Emotion and motivation. A state with a trigger, a bodily change and an action tendency.

objects.label: Appraisal and basic-emotion accounts
objects.text: MS.O.A1.4.1 Appraisal accounts and basic-emotion accounts, as rival answer-families.

objects.label: Motivation and reward
objects.text: MS.O.A1.4.2 Motivation and reward as process claims. The tissue (orbitofrontal cortex, vmPFC, ventral striatum) is MS.O.A2.3.

objects.label: Thought, language and judgement
objects.text: MS.O.A1.5 Thought, language and judgement.

objects.label: Concepts and categories
objects.text: MS.O.A1.5.1 Concepts and categories.

objects.label: Judgement heuristics and biases
objects.text: MS.O.A1.5.2 Judgement heuristics (availability, representativeness, anchoring; Tversky and Kahneman 1974). They are biases relative to a stated normative model. The rule of thumb used by an analyst is a different sentence, in the register.

objects.label: Psycholinguistic processing
objects.text: MS.O.A1.5.3 Psycholinguistic processing (comprehension, production). The grammar itself is LN.

objects.label: Creativity and problem solving
objects.text: MS.O.A1.5.4 Creativity and problem solving (APA Div. 10 home). The aesthetic verdict is AR.

objects.label: RETIRED: see ED
objects.text: MS.O.A1.5.5 RETIRED in Phase 2.1 (ID not reused). Learning claims under an educational arrangement, including physics and mathematics education (MSC 97), are ED.O.A2–A4. MS keeps the general mechanism of learning and memory in MS.O.A1.5.

objects.label: Nervous systems
objects.text: MS.O.A2 Nervous systems

objects.label: Neurons, glia and synapses
objects.text: MS.O.A2.1 Neurons, glia and synapses.

objects.label: Action potential
objects.text: MS.O.A2.1.1 Action potential: an all-or-none spike, given a threshold depolarisation of an excitable membrane.

objects.label: Chemical and electrical synapses
objects.text: MS.O.A2.1.2 Chemical and electrical synapses; excitation and inhibition.

objects.label: Glia
objects.text: MS.O.A2.1.3 Glia: astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, microglia and their signalling roles (SfN Theme B).

objects.label: Plasticity
objects.text: MS.O.A2.2 Plasticity.

objects.label: LTP and LTD
objects.text: MS.O.A2.2.1 Long-term potentiation and depression, as candidate mechanisms of learning. A changed synapse is not yet a memory; the memory is MS.O.A1.3.

objects.label: Circuits and systems
objects.text: MS.O.A2.3 Circuits and systems.

objects.label: Sensory and motor pathways
objects.text: MS.O.A2.3.1 Sensory and motor pathways.

objects.label: Hypothalamus and homeostasis
objects.text: MS.O.A2.3.2 Hypothalamus and homeostasis.

objects.label: Valuation circuits
objects.text: MS.O.A2.3.3 Valuation circuits: orbitofrontal cortex, vmPFC, ventral striatum. "Limbic system" is a contested grouping and is not used as a cell.

objects.label: Localisation
objects.text: MS.O.A2.3.4 Localisation as a starting map; a function is usually a circuit.

objects.label: Development of the nervous system
objects.text: MS.O.A2.4 Development of the nervous system.

objects.label: Overproduction and pruning
objects.text: MS.O.A2.4.1 Overproduction and pruning.

objects.label: Critical and sensitive periods
objects.text: MS.O.A2.4.2 Critical and sensitive periods, with their measured windows.

objects.label: Persons
objects.text: MS.O.A3 Persons

objects.label: Personality
objects.text: MS.O.A3.1 Personality.

objects.label: Five-factor model (HEXACO rival)
objects.text: MS.O.A3.1.1 Five-factor model as the common answer. HEXACO (six factors; Ashton and Lee 2007) is the rival (CONTESTED).

objects.label: Person–situation debate
objects.text: MS.O.A3.1.2 Person–situation debate: both variances are measured.

objects.label: Intelligence and abilities
objects.text: MS.O.A3.2 Intelligence and abilities.

objects.label: g factor
objects.text: MS.O.A3.2.1 g as a statistical factor (Spearman 1904), not a thing seen.

objects.label: Heritability of intelligence
objects.text: MS.O.A3.2.2 Heritability of intelligence: a variance fraction in a stated population, environment and time, broad (H²) or narrow (h²). The quantitative-genetics result uses BI.O.A4.

objects.label: Life-course development
objects.text: MS.O.A3.3 Life-course development.

objects.label: Stage theories
objects.text: MS.O.A3.3.1 Stage theories as ideal types.

objects.label: Attachment classification
objects.text: MS.O.A3.3.2 Attachment classification (Ainsworth; Main and Solomon).

objects.label: Ageing
objects.text: MS.O.A3.3.3 Ageing and adult development.

objects.label: Psychopathology (process account)
objects.text: MS.O.A3.4 Psychopathology. The psychological process account of distress and disability.

objects.label: DSM-5-TR and ICD-11 categories
objects.text: MS.O.A3.4.1 Diagnostic categories as conventions: DSM-5-TR (APA 2022) and ICD-11 (WHO, in force 2022). The category is W12.

objects.label: RDoC
objects.text: MS.O.A3.4.2 RDoC as the process-first alternative (CONTESTED as a basis for classification).

objects.label: Interactions
objects.text: MS.O.A4 Interactions

objects.label: Social influence
objects.text: MS.O.A4.1 Social influence. Conformity, obedience and bystander effects, each with its replication record (Burger 2009; Fischer et al. 2011 meta-analysis on bystanders). Environment–behaviour claims (APA Div. 34) sit here.

objects.label: Social cognition
objects.text: MS.O.A4.2 Social cognition. Attribution; the fundamental attribution error (Ross 1977), flagged as weaker in non-WEIRD samples (Henrich et al. 2010).

objects.label: Attitudes
objects.text: MS.O.A4.3 Attitudes. Cognitive dissonance (Festinger 1957), with self-perception as the rival account. Consumer attitudes (APA Div. 23) sit here; BU.O.A4.1 uses them.

objects.label: Groups and relationships
objects.text: MS.O.A4.4 Groups and relationships. Small groups, roles, norms, status; couples and families; conversation as turn-taking; human–animal interaction (CONTESTED; alternative BI.O.A3).

objects.label: Self and identity
objects.text: MS.O.A4.5 Self and identity. The self as a role taken toward others; identity as a claimed category; body and embodiment. The category's distribution is MS.O.A5.1.

objects.label: Social structures
objects.text: MS.O.A5 Social structures

objects.label: Positions and inequality
objects.text: MS.O.A5.1 Positions and inequality. Status, role, role conflict. Inequality as a residual in life chances after stated controls. Bases include class, race, gender, sexuality and disability.

objects.label: Organisations
objects.text: MS.O.A5.2 Organisations. Weberian bureaucracy (rule, file, career); informal structure. PO.O.A2 uses it for state bureaucracy.

objects.label: Institutions and culture
objects.text: MS.O.A5.3 Institutions and culture. An institution is a repeated, taken-for-granted pattern: family, market, state, religion, school, media, science. Culture is shared meaning in use. Consumption as practice sits here. A paper merely set in a church or school is a sector instance.

objects.label: Populations
objects.text: MS.O.A5.4 Populations. Births, deaths, migration and their rates; life table; cohort. Human population is owned here; non-human population dynamics are BI.O.A5.

objects.label: Collective action and change
objects.text: MS.O.A5.5 Collective action and change. Social movements that target a norm or an organisation. A movement contesting authority is PO.O.A3.3 (CONTESTED target rule). The free-rider result is EC.O.A5.3. Differentiation, diffusion, globalisation. Named theories of history (Marxian, functionalist) are answer-families, reconstructed under MS.M.3.

Psychophysical function with d′ and c, over a stated range
warrants.defeaters: Criterion shift read as sensitivity; out-of-range use

warrants.standard: Effect survives no-report and demand controls
Double dissociation; acquisition and extinction with controls
warrants.defeaters: Single dissociation; ceiling or floor; pseudo-conditioning

warrants.standard: Bias shown against an explicit norm; learning effect in a controlled trial
warrants.defeaters: Wrong normative model; ecological rationality; teaching-to-the-test

warrants.standard: Necessity and sufficiency tests converge with recording
Lesion or stimulation convergent with recording
Reliable measurement with invariance across groups
g loadings; heritability with stated population

warrants.warrant: W12 for the category; W4 for the process
warrants.standard: Inter-rater reliability; process measure predicts course
Pattern shown beyond any one member
Comparative-historical trace; practice traced to record
Registers or census with coverage stated

Neuroscience; cognitive neuroscience; neuropsychology; behavioural neuroscience

sections.governing_thought: Mind, brain and society is exhausted by four faces of one pyramid: objects, methods, warrants and bridges. Its objects are mental processes, nervous systems, persons, interactions and social structures.
sections.key_line:
Logic: inductive. Plural noun: units. Dimension: the unit the claim is about. Order: structural, from the smallest unit that bears a mental claim to the largest pattern.

1. Mental processes
2. Nervous systems
3. Persons
4. Interactions
5. Social structures

Boundary sentences kept from v1. The ion channel is neuroscience. The report of a memory is psychology. The distribution of that report across a class is sociology. Social psychology is the interaction unit asked with psychological methods. Cognitive neuroscience is the process unit asked with neural measures.
sections.assignment_rules:
1. A neural correlate is evidence for a process claim, not the process. It is labelled a correlate until a mechanism is shown.
2. The ion channel and the spike are MS.O.A2.1. The cell as a living unit is BI. The equilibrium potential uses CH.O.A3.3.
3. A diagnostic category is a convention (W12) at MS.O.A3.4.1. Disorder as function failure, treatment and trials are MD.O.A1. Treatment outcome is MD; MS.O.A3.4 cites it.
4. Psychoanalytic theory is an answer-family at MS.O.A1 or MS.O.A3, reconstructed under MS.M.3. Folk psychology is in the register.
5. The availability heuristic as a claim about people is MS.O.A1.5.2. The analyst's rule of thumb is MS.M.H. They are two sentences.
6. Heritability as a quantitative-genetic quantity is owned by BI.O.A4. MS.O.A3.2.2 uses BI.O.A4.
7. An institution as a pattern is MS.O.A5.3. A paper merely set in a church or school is a sector instance.
8. A movement targeting a norm or organisation is MS.O.A5.5. A movement contesting authority uses PO.O.A3.3. The free-rider result uses EC.O.A5.3.
9. Market as allocation is EC.O.A2; market as institution is MS.O.A5.3. Authority is PO.O.A2.
10. Human population is MS.O.A5.4. EC.O.A2.5 (labour supply) uses it. Non-human population is BI.O.A5.
11. Reference-dependent choice as a model of the economic agent is EC.O.A1.3. The bias as a mental process is MS.O.A1.5.2. Strategic exploitation of a bias against a reacting party is ST.O.A5.2.
12. A learning claim under an educational arrangement, including physics and mathematics education research (MSC 97), is ED. A claim about the mechanism of learning, independent of any arrangement, is MS.O.A1.5. The theorem or law taught is MA or PH.
13. Dated claims about past psychologists are HI. The reconstruction of a past theory as an answer is MS.M.3.
14. Audit-to-v2 ID map: A1.5 judgement → A1.5.2; A1.4 memory → A1.3; A1.6 emotion → A1.4; A1.7 consciousness → A1.2.2; A2.5 computational → MS.M.4; A5.3 organisation → A5.2; A5.4 institution and A5.5 culture → A5.3; A5.6 population → A5.4; A5.7 change → A5.5.

sections.crosswalk:
Authorities: APA divisions; ASA sections; SfN themes. Lists and statuses are taken from the audit, which checked apa.org, asanet.org and sfn.org in October 2026. I did not re-check them.

**APA divisions (54; numbered 1–56, 4 and 11 vacant).** Refused (5): Div. 2 Teaching of Psychology (pedagogy), 18 Public Service (guild), 31 State/Provincial Association Affairs (guild), 42 Independent Practice (guild), 52 International (area). The audit's ten "missing" divisions now land:

|---|---|---|

| 14 | Industrial and Organizational | MS.B.C4 |
| 15 | Educational | refused to ED (uses MS.O.A1.5 for mechanism) |

Remaining divisions keep the audit's homes (§5a). Elsewhere (4): 21 → EN human factors; 24 → PL; 28 and 55 → MD. **Coverage: 49 of 49 eligible land (45 home, 4 elsewhere); 5 of 54 refused.**

**ASA sections (55 listed).** Refused (5): Asia and Asian America (area), Global MENA (area), Creative Sociology (in formation), Sociological Practice and Public Sociology (practice), Teaching and Learning (pedagogy). Elsewhere (3): Peace, War and Social Conflict and Political Sociology → PO; Human Rights → PO/LA. The audit's nine missing sections now land: Animals and Society → MS.O.A4.4 (CONTESTED, BI.O.A3); Communication, IT and Media → MS.B.C5; Consumers and Consumption → MS.O.A5.3; Disability → MS.O.A5.1; Environmental → MS.O.A5.3 (state of the environment EA); Global and Transnational → MS.O.A5.5; History of Sociology → MS.M.3; Science, Knowledge and Technology → MS.O.A5.3 (philosophy of science PL); Body and Embodiment → MS.O.A4.5. **Coverage: 50 of 50 eligible; 5 of 55 refused.**

**SfN themes (A–K, 11).** A, B, E, F, G, H, I land in MS.O.A1–A2; J Techniques lands in Face M; C and D land in MD; K lands in MS.M.3 (history) with ethics refused to PL. **Coverage: 11 of 11.**

No authority class called "Other" is used as a cell.
sections.validation:
Sizes: key line 5; Face O cells 28 (5 A-level + 23 sub-cells: A1 5, A2 4, A3 4, A4 5, A5 5); named objects at third level 30 (inside sub-cells, sharing their W rows); M roles 5; heuristics 6 (outside count); W rows 28; B bridges 5.

Key-line members, word for word: Mental processes · Nervous systems · Persons · Interactions · Social structures. The governing thought lists the same five in lower case.

- Vertical. Units answer what is claimed. Methods answer how. Lesion, imaging and computational modelling moved out of Face O.
- Horizontal. One dimension at each level; every key line has 4–5 members.
- OPEN. Whether consciousness research needs its own warrant beyond W4/W9. Replication status of social-influence effects. Whether RDoC should replace category-first classification.
- CONTESTED. Psychopathology process account (alternative: MD.O.A1 owns all). Forgetting mechanism. Five-factor versus HEXACO. Movement target rule (alternative: PO owns all movements). Human–animal interaction (alternative: BI.O.A3).
